title: Volume Smoothing & Burst Hedge Pilot: Flexible per-vector pricing for Embeddings + Rerank
creator: Asha Patel
description: Proposal for a controlled pilot that introduces a ‘volume smoothing’ billing construct and a small burst-credit hedge for embeddings + reranking workloads. Goal is to decouple per-vector unit price from short-term batch variability while preserving revenue predictability and providing enterprise-friendly contract language and QSA artifacts.
hypothesis: If we offer a flexible commitment block (monthly base + smoothing buffer) with an explicit burst-credit allowance and graduated per-vector price tiers that normalize across batch sizes, then customers will accept higher committed spend and churn on price-sensitive reranking workloads will decrease by >10% for pilot cohort.
experiment_design:
- Pilot cohort: 12 existing mid-market customers that run high-frequency rerank pipelines and 8 enterprise prospects flagged by Sales.
- Pricing construct: monthly commitment (committed vectors) + smoothing buffer (percentage of commit, e.g., 15%) + burst credits at a defined premium.
- Metering: count vectors at tokenization stage; batch-aware attribution ensures batch discounts apply to in-buffer traffic first.
- Offer 3 plans (Bronze/Silver/Gold) with different smoothing percentages and burst credit rates.
- Contract: 3-month pilot term, early-exit with prorated consumption reconciliation.
- QSA prep: provide sample QSA answers, indicate no change to data residency or encryption controls.
pricing_matrix_example:
Plan: Bronze | Commit 100M vectors/mo | Smoothing 10% | Base price $0.000012/vector | Burst price $0.000018/vector
Plan: Silver | Commit 500M vectors/mo | Smoothing 15% | Base price $0.000010/vector | Burst price $0.000015/vector
Plan: Gold | Commit 2B vectors/mo | Smoothing 20% | Base price $0.0000085/vector | Burst price $0.000012/vector
Notes: Effective per-vector cost modeled across observed batch-size distributions; larger batch sizes realize lower tokenization overhead and thus reduced effective cost to Redwood.
billing_mechanics:
- Ingest counts vectors in realtime; committed consumption consumed first, smoothing buffer consumed next, bursts charged against burst credits; burst credits can be pre-purchased or invoiced at month-end.
- Metering must expose per-route vector counts and batch-size histograms to Console and the billing export.
- Grace rules: smoothing buffer replenishes daily pro-rata; burst overage triggers alerts and optional auto-topup.
metrics:
- Primary: committed uptake (USD) and churn rate vs control cohort (-10% target churn), commit-to-usage ratio (target 0.75-1.25), average per-vector revenue vs baseline (+5% target), percent of consumption billed as burst (<8% target).
- Secondary: partner sales cycle length for contract acceptance, legal/QSA turnaround time, support volume during pilot.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alignment and eng tickets for metering & billing exports (2 sprints). 2) Legal + RevOps template updates and QSA artifacts (1 sprint). 3) Recruit pilot customers (Sales + CSM). 4) Soft launch with 3 customers for 4 weeks (monitor, iterate). 5) Expand to full pilot cohort for 12 weeks. 6) Readout and decision (go/no-go) with pricing recommendation.
contract_qsa_notes:
- Add contract appendix with explicit smoothing definition, burst-credit accounting, and reconciliation process.
- Provide QSA packet: network/topology diagram, KMS usage description, encryption-at-rest/in-transit, SOC-like controls summary, sample TLS cert expiration policy, and a section on metering and audit logs availability.
- Add clause for data handling: no model training on customer data, retention windows configurable per customer, and logging retention policy.
open_questions: Should smoothing be expressed as a percentage or an absolute vector allowance?
How to model and price for mixed workloads where rerank and embedding vectors have different per-vector compute costs?
Billing export schema changes required for downstream ingestion by Finance?
What minimum contract language will Legal accept for pilot customers?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly generous smoothing leads to revenue leakage. Mitigation: cap smoothing utilization and require auto-topup settings.
Risk: Metering inaccuracies during transition. Mitigation: reconcile with retroactive adjustments and transparent audit logs.
Risk: QSA turnaround slows pilot. Mitigation: proactively prepare QSA packet and reserve security SME hours.
Risk: Customer confusion about burst credits. Mitigation: add clear Console UX and sample invoice preview in the trial.
success_criteria: - >= 60% of pilot customers convert to committed plans after pilot; - Net revenue per pilot customer >= baseline or upward; - Legal approves contract appendix without major edits; - Billing exports processed cleanly by Finance and match internal metering within 0.5% after reconciliation.
